clue.text: Have a late meal with reporters to make check

parts.note: to sup is to eat supper, a light meal late in the evening
the press is the body of newspaper reporters

explanation.surface: Someone dines late with journalists in order to keep them in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or quell it, the same restraint as stifling it.

clue.text: Guard dog-watch out!

indicators.note: the word for watching is spread out so that the dog can sit inside it

parts.note: to watch is to see
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A warning shouted to a guard dog on its watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' asks for SEE to open up around CUR, giving SE-CUR-E; the dash makes 'Guard dog' look like one phrase, but 'Guard' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard a thing is to make it safe and protected.

clue.text: Quick game for inclusion in fitness training

indicators.note: says the game is to be included inside the letters for fitness training

parts.note: PT is physical training, school exercise classes
a romp is a lively playful game

explanation.surface: A fast game slotted into a gym session.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt and quick both mean done without delay.

clue.text: Running water affected her in an odd way

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are affected, that is altered, as the closing 'in an odd way' confirms

explanation.surface: A stream made a woman behave strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' with 'in an odd way' rearranges HER IN; the river is the great European river through Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a body of running water, and this is one of Europe's major rivers.

clue.text: "Look like the innocent flower, but be the — under 't." Shakespeare (Macbeth)

definitions.text: "Look like the innocent flower, but be the — under 't." Shakespeare (Macbeth)

parts.words: "Look like the innocent flower, but be the — under 't." Shakespeare (Macbeth)
parts.note: a fill-in: Lady Macbeth tells her husband to seem harmless while hiding a deadly creature beneath, and the missing word is that creature

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: the solver supplies the missing word from Lady Macbeth's advice in Act 1 of Macbeth.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word names a snake, the creature lurking unseen under the flower in Lady Macbeth's image.

clue.text: Express approval when addressed

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a letter addressed and posted has been sent

explanation.surface: Someone shows they agree on being spoken to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'addressed' looks like 'spoken to', but read as an addressed letter it means posted, SENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeing formally to something is giving it your consent.

clue.text: Pottery having novel article in stock

indicators.note: the new article is placed inside the word for stock

parts.note: a store is a stock of goods
novel means new
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Crockery with a new item kept in the shop's stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but is the adjective, NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoneware is a dense, hard type of pottery fired at high heat.

clue.text: Pole taken in by a schoolboy from the Baltic

indicators.note: the pole is absorbed inside the word for the schoolboy

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil at Eton, the English boarding school
S stands for the south pole

explanation.surface: A Polish man is fooled by a public schoolboy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, but it is a magnetic pole, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is one of the three Baltic states, so a person from there comes from the Baltic.

clue.text: There's great potential in Ed ward which should be correctly guided

indicators.note: the letters of the word great have the potential to become something else when rearranged

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward, printed here split in two

explanation.surface: A ward named Edward has great promise if properly steered.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text splits Edward as 'Ed ward'; its pet name TED follows TARGE, the anagram of GREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimed precisely at a goal, as a missile or a campaign is steered.

clue.text: Crooks may well be spotted in church

definitions.text: Crooks may well be spotted in church

parts.words: Crooks may well be spotted in church
parts.note: the crooks are not criminals but the hooked staffs bishops carry in services

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooks' suggests villains seen at a service; the crooks meant are bishops' staffs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's staff shaped like a shepherd's hook is carried in church ceremonies.

clue.text: Delay to rile constituents

indicators.note: the parts of the words to rile are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Stalling in order to annoy the voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' looks like voters but signals that the letters of TO RILE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To delay is to linger or hang about idly.

clue.text: Staunch and really good man given work

parts.note: a saint is a really good man, abbreviated St
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A loyal and virtuous man is given a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch' looks like the adjective 'loyal'; it is the verb, to stem a flow of blood.
explanation.definitionFit: To staunch bleeding is to halt it.

clue.text: What agents should do about now

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the present is now

explanation.surface: A remark about the duty of agents at the present time.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents act on behalf of their clients, speaking for them.

clue.text: He will be seen before going around Northern Ireland

indicators.note: the word for before encircles the abbreviation for Northern Ireland

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone will be seen before travelling round Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'He' is the British premium bond computer, nicknamed as if a person, which picks winning numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, so a 'he'; it is also the name of the machine choosing British premium bond prizes.

clue.text: Spy-mole

definitions.meaning: to spy is to catch sight of
a mole is a small dark blemish on the skin

explanation.definitionFit: To spy a thing is to notice it; a mole is a small mark on the skin.

clue.text: A wild creature in sound environment playing about

indicators.note: the sound forms the surroundings of the wild creature, enclosing it

parts.note: a ping is a short ringing sound
an otter is a wild river animal

explanation.surface: An animal frolicking in a noisy habitat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pottering is busying oneself idly, doing small tasks without purpose.

clue.text: The French female caught in the head's embrace is calm

indicators.note: the head's letters hold the other pieces inside them

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
la is the French feminine word for the
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman held by the headmistress is soothed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests a head teacher, but it is the top of the skull, PATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To calm someone angry is to pacify them.

clue.text: Quietly came down as promised

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
lighted means settled or came down, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: Something landed softly as had been foretold.
explanation.definitionFit: To plight one's troth is to pledge it, so a pledged thing has been promised.

clue.text: No rating may be without instruction

indicators.note: the words no rating may become other words when rearranged

explanation.surface: Having no grade could mean a person has not been taught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' signals that NO RATING can be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without instruction lacks knowledge, being untaught.

clue.text: The girl working out to get slimmer

indicators.note: the letters of the words the girl are worked into a different order

explanation.surface: A young woman exercising to lose weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working out' suggests the gym but rearranges THE GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: Slimmer means less heavy, weighing less.

clue.text: Bring up the right to a listening-device

parts.note: r stands for right
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Raising the matter of rights with a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring up' looks like raising a subject; it means raising children.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up a child is to rear it.

clue.text: From June educational establishments will have such a requirement

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within the run of letters in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Colleges will need something from June onwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of juNE EDucational.
explanation.definitionFit: A need is something required.

clue.text: Breaking down in tears is not so good

indicators.note: the letters of in tears break down and reform in a new order

explanation.surface: Collapsing into weeping is worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking down' looks like crying, but rearranges IN TEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nastier is more unpleasant, so less good.

clue.text: Traitor, one on an allowance

parts.note: a rat is a deserter or traitor
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A traitor is put on a fixed allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed share or allocation of food or goods.

clue.text: A six-footer's heavy wooden mallet

definitions.meaning: an insect has six legs, a cryptic way to describe one
the word is also a name for a large wooden hammer or rammer

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a six-legged insect and a heavy wooden hammer used for driving wedges.

clue.text: Note nothing is on hand

parts.note: G is a musical note
love means nil in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A note saying no money is available.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on hand' sounds like 'available'; literally it is a thing worn on the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: It is worn on the hand, a fitted covering for fingers and palm.

clue.text: Fool round-call about a col, league

parts.note: an ass is a fool
O is round in shape

indicators.note: the word for call goes round the a

parts.note: to cite is to call, as a witness is cited

explanation.surface: A clown goes round phoning a team-mate.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text breaks colleague as 'col, league'. 'about' puts CITE around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague is a partner at work.

clue.text: Music composed by church worker

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A tune written by someone who works for a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chant is a simple sung melody, as used in church services.

clue.text: Dreadful tease interrupting a jerk

indicators.note: the tease breaks into the jerk, sitting inside it

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk
to rag is to tease

explanation.surface: Mocking someone mid-twitch is awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic events are dreadful, calamitous ones.

clue.text: He shouldn't be a member of more than one union

definitions.text: He shouldn't be a member of more than one union

parts.words: He shouldn't be a member of more than one union
parts.note: the union is not a trade union but marriage, and belonging to two is the crime

explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests trade unions; it means marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who marries while already married commits a crime of double wedlock.

clue.text: The weakness of the old Venetian official receiving thanks

indicators.note: the Venetian official takes in the thanks

parts.note: the doge was the elected ruler of Venice
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: An elderly Venetian ruler grows feeble while being thanked.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is the feebleness of mind of old age.

clue.text: No recent reform is material

explanation.surface: A claim that there has been no reform lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' signals rearranging NO RECENT.
